<blockquote>
This page is about '''Amplified Weapons'''. For information about '''Amplifications''' themselves, see also [[Amplification]].
</blockquote>

'''Amplified Weapons''' are a set of weapons that can be upgraded to '''Level 5''', unlocking '''Amplification''' slots that allow raiders to modify weapon functionality.

== Requirements ==
To upgrade weapons to Level 5 and activate Amplifications, raiders must upgrade the following [[Workshop|workshops]]:
* '''[[Gunsmith]]''' Level 4
* [[Research Station|'''Research Station''']] Level 4

== Upgrading ==
Upgrading a weapon to Level 5 requires a specific '''Amplification Module''' matching the weapon's base rarity tier:

{| class="wikitable" style="text-align: center;"
! Rarity Tier !! Required Upgrade Material
|-
| Common || [[Amplification Module Mk. I]]
|-
| Uncommon || [[Amplification Module Mk. II]]
|-
| Rare || [[Amplification Module Mk. III]]
|-
| Epic || [[Amplification Module Mk. IV]]
|-
| Legendary || [[Amplification Module Mk. V]]
|}

Amplification Modules can be acquired from:

* the [[Fallen Emperor]] using an [[Emperor Gateway Conduit]] on [[Pendola Pass]],
* the cargo inside the [[ARC Frigate (lore)|ARC Frigate]] during the [[ARC Frigate]] event.

Upon reaching Level 5, all weapons immediately gain '''+70 Max Durability'''.
== Repairing ==
Repairing Level 5 weapons require [[Amplified Fragments]]. Repair buffs acquired from [[Expedition|expeditions]] are percentage based, so Level 5 weapons greatly benefit from it.

Knocked out raiders drop amplified weapons with their durability reduced to 10%.

== System Mechanics ==
Once a weapon reaches Level 5, players can select and activate available Amplifications. Once an Amplification is activated, it cannot be removed or changed.

Certain amplifications may be unavailable:

* until the corresponding [[Amplified Research]] is completed in the [[Research Station]],
* until prior amplifications are activated first (e.g., ''Charged Burst'' requires ''Increased Burst''),
* because another amplification conflicts with it (e.g., ''Burst-Fire'' locks out ''Full-Auto'').
